preamble: The wordplay of each clue contains an extra letter, not required for its solution. Twelve of the clues lack a definition and are incorrectly numbered. Their 12 solutions fall into two groups, each with a common theme. When the clues for these 12 solutions are correctly numbered and properly placed, the ‘extra’ letters from all 32 clues in order spell out a description of the exercise, with a label for each.

messages.text: A RECIPROCAL ARRANGEMENT WINE OF NOTE

clue.text: Friend's mother — and what she may pour

parts.note: MA is the everyday short word for a mother
a mother pouring for the family pours tea

explanation.surface: A pal's mum, and the pot of tea she might pour out for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother and her tea run together as MATEA; per the preamble one letter is surplus, and dropping the final A leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a close companion, the British word for a pal or buddy.

clue.text: Stubborn traditionalist parent attacks from behind, grabbing letter

indicators.note: the mother and her muggings close round the Greek letter, holding it between them

parts.note: mum is the British word for mother
a mugger typically assaults a victim from behind
psi is the 23rd letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A mother assaults people from behind and snatches their mail.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM, PSI and MUGS run together as MUMPSIMUGS; the G is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mumpsimus is someone who clings to an old error or custom despite being shown it is wrong.

clue.text: Vocal abnormality Eugene and Tito corrected

indicators.note: the two names are put right by being rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men, Eugene and Tito, have their speech impediments treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of the two names contain one E more than the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue-tie is a short frenulum restricting the tongue, which can impede clear speech.

clue.text: Being divine, Mork's no way of working Orson out

indicators.note: working Orson out suggests puzzling him out, so his letters and the leftovers are rearranged

parts.note: Mork, the alien of Mork & Mindy, with no MO, modus operandi or way of working, leaves RK
Orson is Mork's unseen superior on the planet Ork, taken here letter by letter

explanation.surface: A TV alien, with no method to hand, tries to fathom his boss Orson.
explanation.walkthrough: MORK loses MO to leave RK; that pair with ORSON is rearranged, and one R is the clue's surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kronos, father of Zeus, was a Titan of Greek myth and so a god himself.

clue.text: Mark Lake's about to upset a Native American woman

parts.note: Mk is the standard abbreviation for mark, as in a Mk II model

indicators.note: the lake goes about, around, the reversed word

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word to over so it reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mark is about to knock over a Native American woman at the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch is the Scottish word for a lake, and Mk the usual short form of mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Klootch is a Chinook jargon word, used in the Pacific Northwest, for a Native American woman or wife.

clue.text: College tried to track alternative source of fruit

indicators.note: college and tried follow behind alternative, as a tracker trails its quarry

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a case tried in court has been heard

explanation.surface: A college has tried to follow a different way of growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, C and HEARD give ORCHEARD; the second E is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees, where apples and pears are grown.

clue.text: Forces' Sweetheart engaged in standard sort of service

indicators.note: the singer is engaged within the standard, sitting inside it

parts.note: a norm is the expected standard
Dame Vera Lynn, the singer who entertained British troops in the Second World War

explanation.surface: Vera Lynn, the wartime Forces' Sweetheart, takes part in a routine kind of church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Service suggests church, but it is the tennis or cricket kind: the stroke that starts a point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or cricket an overarm delivery is made with the arm raised above the shoulder.

clue.text: Skill of diplomat overlooking a meeting's minutes

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for diplomatic skill sits above the a, looking down on it

parts.note: tact is the diplomat's skill of handling people without offence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat's tact lets him skim over the record of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: TACT above A gives TACTA; the first T is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is the Latin plural for recorded proceedings, the official minutes of an assembly.

clue.text: Enigmatist's/Enigmatist's

parts.note: the setter speaking of what belongs to him says mine
read as Enigmatist is, the setter's I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: Just the setter's own name twice over, as if signing the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values. MINE then IM gives MINEIM; the E is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note in music, worth two crotchets, and one of the puzzle's theme notes.

clue.text: Old cart unloads in silence

indicators.note: the emptied cart goes in the word for silence

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means silence
a wagon, a cart, unloads the O that stands for old

explanation.surface: An ancient cart is quietly emptied of its load.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes, and its clue swaps places with that of the note value of reciprocal size.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding two standard bottles, one of the puzzle's theme sizes.

clue.text: Large reptile tailed by Troy Baker with a trumpet

indicators.note: the reptile is followed at its tail by the other pieces

parts.note: a croc is a crocodile, a large reptile
T stands for troy, the weight system for precious metals
Chet Baker was an American jazz trumpeter

explanation.surface: A crocodile is followed by a jazz trumpeter, Troy Baker, horn in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values. CROC, T and CHET give CROCTCHET; one C is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a quarter note, the beat of most music, and one of the theme notes.

clue.text: Wounded antelope — it's keeled over

indicators.note: a boat that has keeled over is upside down, so the antelope and the word it's are read backwards

parts.note: the gnu or wildebeest, the crossword's favourite antelope
taken as written, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: An injured antelope topples over on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: GNU plus ITS read backwards gives STIUNG; the I is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stung means hurt, physically by an insect or figuratively by a cutting remark.

clue.text: Baronet reduced risk with mountain crossing

indicators.note: the baronet's letters are crossed, spanned, around the mountain

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a hazard is a risk, reduced by losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A baronet takes fewer risks crossing a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes, and its clue swaps places with that of the note value of reciprocal size.
explanation.definitionFit: A balthazar is a giant wine bottle holding sixteen standard bottles, one of the theme sizes.

clue.text: Series of nightclub reviews

parts.note: a series is an unbroken run, here the run of letters spanning the end of nightclub and the start of reviews

explanation.surface: A run of write-ups of a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values, and its letters run across the two words with one I to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a double whole note, worth two semibreves, one of the theme notes.

clue.text: The person writing this way's healthier when rising

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, me
thus means in this way

indicators.note: printed among the downs, rising reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: haler is the comparative of hale, healthy

explanation.surface: The writer says that, done like this, he feels healthier once he is up.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes. ME, THUS and HALER reversed give METHUSRELAH; the R is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A methuselah is a wine bottle holding eight standard bottles, one of the theme sizes.

clue.text: Attlee's initial malicious words to the House

indicators.note: the initial of a name is its first letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee, the post-war Labour prime minister
snide remarks are slyly malicious

explanation.surface: Attlee's opening speech is a spiteful address to the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The House is not Parliament but a theatre's audience, the house an actor's aside is spoken to. A and SNIDE give ASNIDE; the N is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark an actor speaks to the audience, unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: I must get behind public show of feeling

indicators.note: the I goes behind, after, the other piece

parts.note: a demo, a demonstration, is a public show of feeling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to back a public display of emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes. DEMO then I gives DEMOI; the O is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A demi is a half-bottle of wine, one of the theme sizes.

clue.text: Try to overhear and oversee pad being wrecked

indicators.note: a wrecked pad is torn apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops while supervising a flat being trashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of oversee pad contain one E more than the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation.

clue.text: One shouts angrily about disturbance of the peace they provoke

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the angry shouting goes about, around, the public disorder

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily at length
a riot is a violent disturbance of the peace

explanation.surface: A man yells furiously about a public disturbance that the agitators started.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritants are things that annoy or inflame, so they provoke a reaction.

clue.text: Very drunk, hearty drinker is one farthing short

indicators.note: the drinker downs, takes in, the letter for very

parts.words: hearty drinker is one farthing short
parts.note: a quaffer drinks heartily; one F, the abbreviation for the old farthing coin, is lost

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker, plastered, is one farthing short of paying for his round.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values. QUAFFER loses one F and takes in V, giving QUAVFER; the other F is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaver is an eighth note, half a crotchet, and one of the theme notes.

clue.text: Detective positive after second phase

indicators.note: the detective and positive come after second, so its letter leads

parts.note: TEC is short for detective
P is the abbreviation for positive, as on a battery terminal

explanation.surface: An investigator turns optimistic once the second stage of a case begins.
explanation.walkthrough: S, TEC and P give STECP; the C is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a process, just as a phase is.

clue.text: What tenant pays, with nothing to it

indicators.note: nothing comes along with the rent, attached at its end

parts.note: a tenant pays the rent, taken whole with its article
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Rent paid by a tenant, though the place is not worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RENT plus O gives THERENTO; the N is the surplus letter. The definition hides in the phrase nothing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal, legal word meaning to that or to it.

clue.text: Spent penny (one fare in US car)

indicators.note: the one and the fare go in the American car

parts.note: auto is the American word for a car
I is the Roman numeral one
to fare is to do, as in how did you fare

explanation.surface: Someone used the toilet, then paid a cab fare in an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: To spend a penny is a British euphemism for using the toilet, which is the surface's misdirection; here the words are simply money spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent has been paid out, handed over in payment.

clue.text: Virginia's turned over in central area of Times Square, unusually

indicators.note: the reversed state goes in among the other letters
the letters are arranged in an unusual order
the central area of a word is all but its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: turned over means the state's letters are read backwards

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Virginia's flag is flipped in the middle of Times Square, an unusual sight.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values, and its clue swaps places with that of the wine bottle of reciprocal size.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a sixteenth note, half a quaver, one of the theme notes.

clue.text: Topless escort busy, I picked up hunks

indicators.note: a busy escort is all over the place, so its remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: escort with its top letter lost

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A topless escort is busy while I pick up muscular men.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunks is an old word for a miser, not a muscleman. SCORT rearranged as SCROT with EGO reversed gives SCROTOGE; the T is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunks is an archaic word for a miser, and Scrooge is fiction's archetypal miser.

clue.text: Having got rid of Eastern look, back bar swinging

parts.words: Having got rid of Eastern look
parts.note: to look is to seem, as in you look tired; it gets rid of one E, for Eastern

indicators.note: back means the bar and the swinging are read in reverse

parts.note: a lever is a rigid bar used for prising
a swinger who goes both ways is bi

explanation.surface: Someone drops their Oriental look and swings back on a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of note values. SEM then LEVER plus BI reversed gives SEMIBREVEL; the L is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a whole note, worth four crotchets, one of the theme notes.

clue.text: May wants a Victory in Europe to lift femme fatale

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters makes them read upwards

parts.note: Theresa May was the Prime Minister, PM, when this puzzle appeared in 2018
taken as written
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in May 1945

explanation.surface: May hopes a VE Day celebration will lift a seductive woman's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: PM, A and VE read upwards give EVAMP; the E is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a seductive woman who exploits men, the same type as a femme fatale.

clue.text: Officially inspect force on small island

parts.note: VIS is the Latin word for force, as in vis major
an ait or eyot is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: An inspector arrives in force on a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: VIS on AIT gives VISAIT; the second A is the surplus letter. An ait is a small river island, such as those on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An official visit, by an inspector or a bishop, is a formal inspection.

clue.text: Task is to bag King Edward range

indicators.note: the task bags, holds inside it, the king

parts.note: a job is a task
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
to range is to roam freely

explanation.surface: The job is to bag up King Edward potatoes in a range of sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes. King Edward looks like the potato, but ER is Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large wine bottle, four standard bottles of champagne, one of the theme sizes.

clue.text: Another showing buttocks but hiding a pot

parts.note: the rear, the backside, but with its a hidden away
an urn is a large pot or vase

explanation.surface: A second broadcast with bare bottoms on display, though a pot conceals something.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding here means the a is tucked away out of sight, so it disappears from the backside word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme, another screening of the same show.

clue.text: Ring reinforces engagement

indicators.note: the ring is put into the battle like reinforcements sent in

parts.note: an engagement is a battle between forces
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring makes an engagement firmer.
explanation.walkthrough: No definition, per the preamble: the answer belongs to a set of wine bottle sizes. O inside BATTLE gives BOATTLE; the A is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard 75cl wine bottle is the unit the theme's other sizes halve and double.

clue.text: Work on discharging matter

parts.note: taken as written
pus is the matter a wound discharges

explanation.surface: A medic works on a wound that is weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: ON and PUS give ONPUS; the N is the surplus letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary composition, a creative piece in a catalogue.
